label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
I used Kilbarrack Van Co on Saturday 17 October for a move from Phibsborough to Drumcondra. It was a two-bed flat, although mostly my own stuff, and the new place was a fourth-floor walk-up with no lift, so it wasn’t the easiest job. I booked through their website and paid a €50 deposit by Revolut. The quote was €340 for up to four hours, with two lads and the van, and the move took around three and a half hours. Other quotes I got were €450 or more, so they were comfortably the best value I found.

They were due to arrive at 9 but got there at 10.30. To be fair, Dessie texted at 8.40 to say the previous job had overrun, so at least I knew what was happening. Still, an hour and a half is a fair wait when you’re sitting on boxes with a cold coffee, ready to go. It didn’t cause me a major problem on the day, but it could have if I’d been working to a tight landlord handover or needed to be out by a particular time. Dessie knocked €40 off afterwards because of the delay, without me asking, which I thought was a decent way of handling it.

Once they arrived, they got stuck in and were easy to deal with. The stairs were awkward, but there was no complaining or dragging the job out. My couch wouldn’t go around the turn on the third floor, and one of the lads, Kev I think, produced an Allen key from his pocket, took the legs off and had it straight in. They also put my bed back together without being asked and took away a flat-pack shelf I didn’t want, which saved me two jobs at the other end. Those bits made a real difference when all I wanted was to get into the new place and stop looking at cardboard boxes.

The one thing I was genuinely disappointed about was my brass floor lamp. Nearly everything else was wrapped in blankets, but the lamp wasn’t, and the base got chipped during the move. It isn’t some expensive designer piece, but it was my nanny’s lamp, so I was a bit gutted. I don’t want that to make the whole move sound like a disaster, because it wasn’t, but it’s worth mentioning for anyone deciding who to book. If you have something fragile, awkwardly shaped or sentimental, I’d point it out before they start and make sure it’s properly wrapped.

So it’s four stars rather than five from me. The lateness and the chipped lamp are why it’s not five, but the price, the work rate and the way Dessie sorted the delay without being chased all count for a lot. I would genuinely use them again and I’d still recommend getting a quote. I’d just allow a bit of breathing room if your moving day has a hard deadline, and make sure anything delicate is wrapped before it goes near the van. And wrap the lamps, lads.
